study: one mid-height bracing level on a 12 m pinned steel column
claim: In this principal-plane model of a 12 m square steel tube, the bare one-wave reference first yielded at 229 kN; with one mid-height lateral brace, the less favourable of two braced crookedness shapes first yielded at 619 kN. Every registered crookedness-size, shape, and brace-height case remained above twice its corresponding one-wave bare reference.

what_is_not_claimed: First yield of the extreme fibre only: not a collapse load, not an ultimate or code design value; the post-yield response was not computed. The result applies to one principal bending plane. No out-of-plane response or biaxial stress interaction was computed. A real column would require adequate restraint in the other direction; this study does not quantify that system. No local buckling of the tube wall, residual stress or twisting. The strut connection is assumed no-slip and its neighbour rigid. The bare reference and the braced column do not carry the same crookedness: a single half-wave, and the less favourable of two braced shapes. The tested strut is about 390 times the closed-form ideal-brace threshold for this elastic model. Therefore 0.5x-2x is a saturated stiff-brace control band, not a stiffness-sensitivity study; much softer braces were not computed.
verification_not_validation: The tangent identities (pi^2 EI/L^2 bare, 4 pi^2 EI/L^2 with the middle held), equilibrium and reaction closure at every first yield, the spring's isolation and energy, the mirror, and the mesh, load-step and tolerance refinement are checks of the solve against itself and against theory for a perfect column. No test of a real braced column is reproduced here.
published_solver_origin: column_fem, column_geometry, inverse_design, fem, geometry, failure and materials are byte-identical to the solver folder of the public three-thresholds package, and config/column_config.json to its config.json
